transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-01
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Arianna Lopez (Redwood AE), Noah Stein (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM); Priya Rao (Celeris CTO), Samir Desai (SRE Lead), Lena Ortiz (PM), Omar Hafez (ML Eng)

Summary:
Quick scoping for a 4-week POC focusing on burst handling, concurrency and token mix. Customer wants to validate average-latency SLOs during traffic spikes and measure cost delta between hosted vs dedicated with quantized model variants. Discussed success criteria, telemetry needed, and an initial benchmark matrix.

Topics covered:
- Workload shape: daily QPS baseline, 95th percentile bursts, sustained concurrency
- Token distribution: average input/output, tail tokens, sample prompts
- Benchmark design: ramp, steady-state, soak, chaos-failure scenarios
- Infra options: hosted API vs dedicated pool vs private VPC + KMS
- Security/compliance checks: SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs
- Timeline & roles for the 4-week POC

Action items (see metadata list)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Arianna: Okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Arianna from Redwood, AE on this account, with Noah our systems engineer and Maya who'll be running the POC operations. Priya, do you want to intro the Celeris folks real quick?
[00:18] Priya: Yeah hi all, Priya here, CTO at Celeris. We're building a multimodal assistant for customer support, lots of short prompts but occasional long context windows for case histories. Samir and Omar will lead infra and ML eng. Lena will own product success.
[00:38] Noah: Great, quick agenda — confirm success criteria, get a traffic profile, then map out benchmark matrix and timing. Does that sound right?
[00:46] Samir: Yep, sounds good. Our top concern is handling the 95th percentile burst — we get sudden ramp-ups from campaigns. Baseline QPS is around 30 qps, but we've seen bursts to 450 qps for 1-3 minutes.
[01:05] Lena: And since we do user history stitching we often have 400-1200 output tokens on some responses. Average output is more like 220 tokens. Inputs are short, around 20-80 tokens.
[01:20] Omar: To add a nuance — about 8% of requests invoke a long retrieval chain that adds pre-pended context of 700-1,500 tokens, which changes latency profiles dramatically.
[01:38] Arianna: That's super helpful. So we should model three traffic tiers: baseline (30 qps), sustained elevated (100-150 qps), and burst (350-500 qps) for short windows, with a long-tail token distribution. We'll propose a benchmark matrix that includes each.
[02:02] Priya: For success criteria, we want p50 < 200ms for short prompts, p95 < 800ms for normal conversation, and p95 < 2.5s during burst for the hosted option. For dedicated we expect tighter latencies.
[02:21] Noah: Quick note — those absolute latencies depend on model choice, quantization, and batch windowing. We'll list a few model candidates and a quantization profile that preserves output quality. Are you open to 4-bit quantized variants for cost testing?
[02:38] Priya: Possibly, but we need to run quality evals on the retrieval-heavy prompts. If quality regresses we'll need fallback to FP16.
[02:47] Maya: One practical ask — can you send a redacted set of 200 representative prompts and a histogram of token lengths? That will let us simulate a realistic token mix.
[02:58] Priya: Yes, we'll export that. Samir will prepare traffic logs.
[03:05] Samir: Note about concurrency — our frontend maintains around 20k websocket connections but active concurrency for inference is usually much lower, around 120 concurrent inferences at baseline with spikes to 1,800 concurrent during flash events.
[03:22] Noah: Important for sizing: concurrency + KV cache locality will change memory pressure. For the POC we'll test a KV cache warm state and cold start to show difference. We'll include measurements of peak GPU memory, KV miss rates, and per-token throughput.
[03:41] Lena: What's Redwood's recommended config for ephemeral bursts? Do you spin up more instances or route to a cheaper model?
[03:49] Arianna: We have two levers — burst capacity using ephemeral instances (dedicated or hosted) and routing to cheaper model variants or lower quantization. For mission-critical queries we can set policy to fall back to a small FP16 model with preserved core intents. We'll show cost/latency tradeoffs in the benchmark results.
[04:10] Priya: Security: we need details on SSO, SAML, KMS integrations and audit logs for compliance. Also data residency for EU users.
[04:21] Maya: We'll send our SOC2 and KMS whitepapers. For Private deployment we support VPC peering and on-prem packages; that will require a separate legal discussion but feasible.
[04:34] Omar: For telemetry, we want token-level cost, per-route latency, and end-to-end traces so we can map slow tails to prompt types. Can Redwood capture HTTP request ids through the pipeline?
[04:44] Noah: Yes, we pass request ids and can surface token-level timing and KV cache hits in Console. We'll add tracing hooks for your logs.
[04:54] Priya: For the benchmark matrix — can you lay out durations? We were thinking: 15m ramp, 30m steady, 5-10m burst, and a 2hr soak to test memory leaks. Is that typical?
[05:10] Noah: Yep that's a common structure. We'll include cold-start runs and a chaos test where we simulate one AZ failure to show fallback behavior. For POC scope we'll run each scenario against hosted and a 2-GPU dedicated pool, and optionally a private VPC if you want to test KMS.
[05:34] Lena: Cost is a big item. We need an estimate of per-1M-token cost for hosted vs dedicated with and without quantization.
[05:44] Arianna: We'll provide ballpark numbers early — dedicated commits significantly lower per-token cost at scale, especially when you enable longer batching and KV cache. We'll include a cost model spreadsheet in the follow-up.
[05:58] Samir: Is there an easy way to replay traffic? We can dump gzip logs but want to make sure tokenization matches your pipeline.
[06:08] Noah: We'll supply a replay harness and a tokenizer shim so your logs map to the token counts we measure; we do have small tokenization diffs sometimes across tokenizer libraries, we'll flag those.
[06:22] Arianna: A few gotchas from other customers — the 95th percentile burst can be dominated by long-context requests, so you may want to protect certain endpoints with rate-limits or prefer model variants for retrieval-heavy flows.
[06:39] Priya: That makes sense. We'll identify sensitive endpoints to treat differently.
[06:45] Omar: For quality gating, we want to define a regression criteria: if BLEU/ROUGE or an internal QA score drops by >2% vs baseline, revert quantization. Is that something Redwood can automate?
[06:56] Noah: We can run A/B comparisons and surface drift alerts via the Console. Quality gating hooks into rollout policies; we can stop a rollout if evals fail.
[07:06] Lena: Timeline — we prefer a 4-week POC: week 0 ingest data and set up env, week 1 run baseline and small-scale tests, week 2 run burst/chaos, week 3 run soak and consolidate results. Does that align?
[07:19] Arianna: Yes, sounds good. We'll prepare a detailed project plan with milestones and owners.
[07:27] Priya: One question — for private deployment does Redwood support bringing-your-own-key (BYOK) with HSM?
[07:33] Maya: Yes, BYOK via KMS/HSM is supported in Private deployments; we'll need to align on key rollover and access policies.
[07:43] Samir: Networking: for VPC peering we need to know ports and egress patterns. Also what telemetry endpoints call home so we can pre-approve in firewall rules.
[07:56] Noah: We'll provide a network whitepaper with IP ranges and ports, and an offline installer checklist for on-prem.
[08:05] Priya: For success criteria recap: acceptable latency thresholds, no more than X% error rate on long-context responses, and a cost per 1M tokens under a target number (TBD). We'll finalize numbers once we see the initial cost sheet.
[08:20] Arianna: Great. We'll produce the benchmark plan and cost sheet. One more thing — can we get a sample of diverse prompts including the long retrieval chain examples? That will help quality evaluation.
[08:32] Priya: Yes, we'll share 200 samples with annotations for which must not lose fidelity.
[08:40] Arianna: Perfect. Any final questions?
[08:44] Lena: Just logistics — who's coordinating the deep-dive?
[08:47] Arianna: Noah will lead the technical deep-dive. Maya will coordinate scheduling and access.
[08:52] Priya: Ok thanks everyone. We'll aim to provide the logs and samples by Monday.
[08:58] Arianna: Thanks, we'll send the plan and calendar invites. Bye!

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-heard acronyms, some speaker attribution simplified; filler words and interruptions preserved.

End of transcript.
